5. Lightning stroke locations on a map (possible postgresql database with postgis for mapping) calculated from sferic data.

Name: Gwyn Griffiths
Suggested Feature Name: Automated within-band check with feedback to station operator
Feature Description: An issue I've encountered, which can be subtle or blatant, is that of spectral clipping in the +/- 5Hz bandwidth (10 Hz sampling rate) used by the RX888 Mk2 stations (and perhaps others?). Accurate measurement of Doppler shift requires a spectrum without instrumental clipping of its high or low skirts. This can occur for a spectrum of modest width (~1 Hz) if the Doppler is substantial - as I see on multihop trans auroral oval WWVH to the UK for example. Or if the spectrum is wide, e.g. two hop sidescatter. Thinking ahead to the Antarctic deployments, checking that stations are using and reporting with adequate sampling rates is important for highest quality reduced data.
General Comments (optional): With existing data I have resorted to clipping the Fourier components of the the other skirt to have a balanced spectrum for Doppler calculation where I've seen this behaviour.

Name: Gwyn Griffiths
Suggested Feature Name: Python API for Doppler, level and frequency spread computations
Feature Description:
Yes please! I have to stress how brilliant the existing quick look spectrograms and digital RF data are. But I'd so like to automate, especially across the midnight boundary so I can easily see local-noon centred plots.
I'd appreciate professionally coded simple analysis tools in Python - my amateur efforts are at https://github.com/g3zil/grapeDRF_doppler_model 
encompassing Doppler shift, level and frequency spread when the spectrogram is unimodal, and the far more difficult tasks of assigning and tracking Doppler shifts when multiple co-propagating modes are present.
General Comments (optional): I have submitted an article to QEX based on https://github.com/g3zil/grapeDRF_doppler_model , if you'd like a copy of the manuscript, let me know.

Name: Gwyn Griffiths
Feature Description: This probably falls under your words, " input on other aspects of the Personal Space Weather Station is also welcome". This feature is what I am currently working on in prep for AGU MacGyver. It is to use automated ray tracing (PyLap at an elevation increment of 0.005?) with a small suite of python scripts I've written / am writing to generate synthetic spectrograms. These spectrograms have the climatology of what rays can propagate from WWV to station X on frequency Y and what Doppler they have. I then know exactly what mode results in what Doppler. My concept is that the synthetic spectrogram would be overlaid (or underlaid) with the measured spectrogram to help elucidate the modes present, find missing modes, show weather vs climate etc etc.

Name: Gwyn Griffiths
Feature Description:
RX888 Mk 2 receivers with WsprDaemon and ka6q-radio software are able to make measurements of the signal levels and, with new code, noise levels at the SMA input to the receiver. But between that SMA connector and the incoming signals there will be site-specific antennas, filters, preamps, splitters etc making the task of estimating the field strength of the incoming signals difficult.
Might there be a few reference sites where the equipment between the RX888 SMA and free space is a) as simple as possible and b) as well calibrated as possible such that these sites could provide field strength estimates? For example a few sites might be equipped with a Rohde and Schwarz HE010 antenna with its well-known calibration. At those sites such an installation could become a 'transfer standard' to calibrate co-located systems e.g. the DX Engineering 'monopole' active antenna.
